scope: One distinct Nara protocol: own Ethereum NaraUSD collateral engine plus NaraUSD+ staking financial requests and claims; not counted as two brands.

lifecycleEvidence.observation: Current primary documentation describes authorized-user mint/redeem and permissionless staking; current app offers Mint, Redeem and Stake and its production Ethereum config binds exact reviewed deployments. Point-in-time unpaused and nonzero caps additionally observed; not continuous liveness or financial safety.

limitations: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, backing, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution, legal eligibility or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory; zero native value required.

Ethereum NaraUSD primary collateral mint/redemption and NaraUSD+ staking only, not BSC bridge tokens, Port/third-party vault curation, issuer minting, rewards management, permits or roles. Current implementation slots observed at block 26257645: NaraUSD 0x87cf5006e1cbf0d35c622c5f1be891b2f71878ea; NaraUSD+ 0x9e1d521894c45fa26e0f06809674037c78e3c1b3. UUPS roles, collateral/MCT, Keyring and silo controls are mutable.

Primary mint/redeem is for Authorized Users under KYC/KYB and configured Keyring credentials/whitelist; blacklists and pause apply. Catalog admission grants no credential, role, approval or legal access. Staking deposits are permissionless subject to blacklist/pause and source minimum-share constraints.

NaraUSD mint pulls supported collateral from msg.sender and mints only to msg.sender through MCT. Redemption burns caller NaraUSD and pays caller selected collateral; allowQueue=false reverts if liquidity is insufficient. Native collateral decimals are normalized to 18; division truncates. Mutable percentage/minimum fees, minimum amounts and per-block limits apply; no caller min-output/deadline parameter exists.

Queued redemption locks caller NaraUSD in the redeem silo; one request per address, NOT a FIFO queue despite primary documentation describing ordered service. Manager can complete opportunistically; caller tryCompleteRedeem can complete own request if liquidity/caps permit. Completion burns escrow and pays caller at current fees; it does not recheck Keyring expiry. Asset removal can block completion. cancelRedeem returns escrow subject to pause/blacklist; updateRedemptionRequest funds/refunds the difference without changing asset. No payout date is guaranteed.

NaraUSD+ deposit/mint pulls caller NaraUSD and issues shares to receiver; 18-decimal underlying/shares, balance-minus-unvested-rewards ERC4626 exchange rate with virtual offsets. Deposit floors shares; mint rounds required assets up. NAV/income originates from offchain payment-financing operations and maker/reviewer/executor controls, not autonomous proof of portfolio value; insurance then staked shares absorb losses, and principal can be lost.

NaraUSD+ cooldown was 604800 seconds (7 days) and both proxies paused=false at the observed block, not continuing availability. Direct withdraw/redeem is structurally disabled while cooldown is nonzero and excluded. cooldownAssets rounds shares up; cooldownShares locks exact caller shares. Both transfer shares into silo and adding to an existing cooldown resets unlock for ALL locked shares. Assets returned by preview are not a fixed future entitlement; shares continue rate exposure until unstake burns at claim-time rate to receiver. cancelCooldown returns locked shares.

Queue and cooldown ledgers explicitly narrow amounts to uint152; callers must keep queued/updated/aggregate locked share amounts within that range. Minimum-share invariants can prevent dust exits. unstake has no top-level pause modifier but calls _withdraw, which enforces pause/blacklists/nonzero/minimum shares. No silo administrative or direct transfer method is admitted.

Primary docs target redemption within 7 days but mention pressure up to roughly 90 days; these are not contract-enforced completion promises. Credit, reserve mix, custody, offchain settlement, mutable fees, freezes and legal/operational loss risks remain. Source and ABI review proves none of the portfolio, backing, yield or solvency claims.

> For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://docs.nara.io/llms.txt). Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://docs.nara.io/nara-protocol/narausd.md).

# NaraUSD

**NaraUSD is a synthetic dollar backed by a portfolio of liquid reserves and short-duration payment-financing positions. It is not a fiat-reserve stablecoin: its value depends on that portfolio performing, on redemption liquidity, and on the controls around both.** It is redeemable for a dollar, freely transferable, and to plug into any venue that accepts an ERC-20. On its own it earns nothing; yield accrues only to NaraUSD+.

#### Minting

Minting is available to Authorized Users: addresses that have completed KYC/KYB with Nara and are screened on-chain at the point of minting. An Authorized User deposits an eligible stablecoin (supported assets) and receives NaraUSD 1:1. Per-block mint limits are enforced in the contract. Anyone else can acquire NaraUSD on supported secondary venues at market price. See Eligibility and onboarding.

#### Redeeming

Authorized Users redeem NaraUSD for an eligible stablecoin at 1:1. The contract burns the NaraUSD and transfers the designated liquid asset.

| Case                           | What happens                                                                                   | Timing                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Request fits the liquid buffer | Processed immediately                                                                          | Instant                                                                                                 |
| Request exceeds the buffer     | Queued on-chain; served in order as the buffer refills from position roll-off and new deposits | Targeted within 7 days; under sustained pressure, up to about 90 days set by the longest position terms |

The queue is public chain state: requests, order and fulfilments are on-chain events. A queued request can be cancelled before fulfilment.

#### What backs it

The liquid buffer is held in stablecoins and on-chain savings products (currently Sky's sUSDS) so that it earns while it waits. The credit portfolio is listed position by position on the Portfolio page. The protocol backing ratio (total assets ÷ supply) is on the [dashboard](https://app.nara.io/transparency).

#### Where it sits in a loss

NaraUSD is senior to NaraUSD+. A portfolio loss is absorbed first by the Insurance Fund, then by the full value of NaraUSD+, and only then by NaraUSD. NaraUSD remains exposed to stablecoin, liquidity, custody, smart-contract, legal and operational risk, which no waterfall addresses. See Risks.

#### Secondary price

NaraUSD can trade above or below a dollar on a DEX. Primary redemption at 1:1 for Authorized Users anchors the price; secondary depth is not guaranteed by Nara.

Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://docs.nara.io/nara-protocol/narausd+.md). # NaraUSD+ **NaraUSD+ is the staked form of NaraUSD. It is an ERC-4626 vault share whose exchange rate against NaraUSD rises as the payment-financing portfolio pays, and it is the token that bears portfolio losses once the Insurance Fund is exhausted.** Yield is variable, is not guaranteed, and depends on borrower draw activity, pricing, settlement timing, credit losses, the reserve mix and fees. #### How yield accrues 1. **Stake.** Deposit NaraUSD into the staking vault and receive NaraUSD+ at the current exchange rate. Staking is permissionless. The rate at launch was 1 NaraUSD+ = 1 NaraUSD. 2. **Earn.** As positions pay, realized income returns to the vault. NAV is calculated off-chain, verified through the maker → reviewer → executor process, and written on-chain as the new exchange rate. Rewards vest into the rate over a set period rather than jumping, and reward issuance can never exceed the on-chain unbacked-mint cap. 3. **Hold.** Each NaraUSD+ is worth more NaraUSD over time. There is nothing to claim and no rebasing balance; the token count stays constant and the rate moves. The live exchange rate is on the [dashboard](https://app.nara.io/transparency). Illustration, with hypothetical rates: a holder who staked 10,000 NaraUSD at a rate of 1.00 and unstakes at 1.04 receives 10,400 NaraUSD before any loss event. A realized credit loss that exceeds the Insurance Fund reduces the rate, so the same holder could receive less than 10,000.\
### Why the NaraUSD+ APR can differ from the portfolio yield The portfolio's yield accrues to the staked share of supply. When the staked ratio is below 100%, the yield on the whole book is distributed over a smaller base, and the NaraUSD+ APR is higher than the blended portfolio yield. #### Unstaking | Stage | What happens | Timing | | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | | Request | Submit an unstaking request. The NaraUSD+ is locked in a silo and continues to accrue at the vault rate during the cooldown. | Immediate | | Cooldown | The protocol uses the window to manage liquidity across positions. | 7 days | | Claim | The NaraUSD+ is burned and NaraUSD is returned at the exchange rate prevailing at claim. | After day 7 | | Exit to stablecoins | Authorized Users then redeem NaraUSD; anyone can sell NaraUSD+ or NaraUSD on secondary venues at market price instead of waiting. | Up to a further 7 days via the primary route | #### Where it sits in a loss NaraUSD+ is the second tier of the loss waterfall. It receives the yield in exchange for taking losses after the Insurance Fund and before NaraUSD. It can lose principal. #### Fees At launch the only deduction from gross strategy yield is the 10% share retained in the Insurance Fund, about 1% of assets a year at the target rate, which stays in the holders' own first-loss buffer. There is no management fee, no performance fee and no mint or redeem fee. Nara will announce any protocol fee here before it takes effect. --- # Agent Instructions This documentation is published with GitBook. devdoc.details: This contract implements an upgradeable proxy. It is upgradeable because calls are delegated to an implementation address that can be changed. This address is stored in storage in the location specified by https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967[EIP1967], so that it doesn't conflict with the storage layout of the implementation behind the proxy.

constructor.details: Initializes the upgradeable proxy with an initial implementation specified by `_logic`. If `_data` is nonempty, it's used as data in a delegate call to `_logic`. This will typically be an encoded function call, and allows initializing the storage of the proxy like a Solidity constructor.

devdoc.details: This contract combines ERC4626 vault with direct collateral minting - Underlying asset: MCT (MultiCollateralToken) - Exchange rate: 1:1 with MCT - Users can mint by depositing collateral (USDC, etc.) - Collateral is converted to MCT, then NaraUSD shares are minted - Redemptions: instant if liquidity available, otherwise queued for solver execution - Users can cancel queued redemption requests anytimeIMPORTANT - ERC4626 Limitations: This contract partially implements ERC4626.      - ERC4626 deposit() and mint() are DISABLED - use mintWithCollateral() instead      - ERC4626 withdraw() and redeem() are DISABLED - use redeem(collateralAsset, naraUsdAmount, allowQueue) instead      - maxDeposit() and maxMint() reflect per-block limits and paused state      - maxWithdraw() and maxRedeem() return 0 (ERC4626 withdraw/redeem are unsupported)      - preview* functions account for fees but the corresponding actions may be disabledIMPORTANT - Redemption Mechanism: The "redemption queue" is NOT an ordered FIFO queue.      It is implemented as a per-user mapping (one active request per user). There is no global      ordering, no "next in line" concept, and no automatic FIFO processing. Can:   - Pause/unpause all operations - COLLATERAL_MANAGER_ROLE: Manages redemption queue execution. Can:   - Complete queued redemptions (completeRedeem, bulkCompleteRedeem)   - Acts as "solver" to process escrowed redemption requests when liquidity becomes available   - Completion order is discretionary (not FIFO) - can complete any user's request opportunistically - MINTER_ROLE: Can mint NaraUSD without collateral backing (for incentives, etc.) - BLACKLIST_MANAGER_ROLE: Can add/remove addresses from blacklist (FULL_RESTRICTED_ROLE) - FULL_RESTRICTED_ROLE: Restriction status (not an operator role). devdoc.details: This contract combines ERC4626 vault with direct collateral minting - Underlying asset: MCT (MultiCollateralToken) - Exchange rate: 1:1 with MCT - Users can mint by depositing collateral (USDC, etc.) - Collateral is converted to MCT, then NaraUSD shares are minted - Redemptions: instant if liquidity available, otherwise queued for solver execution - Users can cancel queued redemption requests anytimeIMPORTANT - ERC4626 Limitations: This contract partially implements ERC4626.      - ERC4626 deposit() and mint() are DISABLED - use mintWithCollateral() instead      - ERC4626 withdraw() and redeem() are DISABLED - use redeem(collateralAsset, naraUsdAmount, allowQueue) instead      - maxDeposit() and maxMint() reflect per-block limits and paused state      - maxWithdraw() and maxRedeem() return 0 (ERC4626 withdraw/redeem are unsupported)      - preview* functions account for fees but the corresponding actions may be disabledIMPORTANT - Redemption Mechanism: The "redemption queue" is NOT an ordered FIFO queue.      It is implemented as a per-user mapping (one active request per user). There is no global      ordering, no "next in line" concept, and no automatic FIFO processing. Completion order is      discretionary by the COLLATERAL_MANAGER_ROLE (solver), who can complete requests opportunistically      via completeRedeem() or bulkCompleteRedeem() when liquidity becomes available.This contract is upgradeable using UUPS proxy patternPrivileged roles: - DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE: Full administrative control. Can:   - Upgrade contract implementation (UUPS)   - Set all configuration parameters (fees, limits, minimums, treasury, Keyring config)   - Redistribute locked amounts from blacklisted users   - Grant/revoke all other roles - GATEKEEPER_ROLE: Emergency controls. Can:   - Pause/unpause all operations - COLLATERAL_MANAGER_ROLE: Manages redemption queue execution. Can:   - Complete queued redemptions (completeRedeem, bulkCompleteRedeem)   - Acts as "solver" to process escrowed redemption requests when liquidity becomes available   - Completion order is discretionary (not FIFO) - can complete any user's request opportunistically - MINTER_ROLE: Can mint NaraUSD without collateral backing (for incentives, etc.) - BLACKLIST_MANAGER_ROLE: Can add/remove addresses from blacklist (FULL_RESTRICTED_ROLE) - FULL_RESTRICTED_ROLE: Restriction status (not an operator role). Addresses with this role:   - Cannot transfer tokens (including via transferFrom)   - Cannot mint or redeem   - Can have their locked balances redistributed by admin

devdoc.details: This contract combines ERC4626 vault with direct collateral minting - Underlying asset: MCT (MultiCollateralToken) - Exchange rate: 1:1 with MCT - Users can mint by depositing collateral (USDC, etc.) - Collateral is converted to MCT, then NaraUSD shares are minted - Redemptions: instant if liquidity available, otherwise queued for solver execution - Users can cancel queued redemption requests anytimeIMPORTANT - ERC4626 Limitations: This contract partially implements ERC4626.      - ERC4626 deposit() and mint() are DISABLED - use mintWithCollateral() instead      - ERC4626 withdraw() and redeem() are DISABLED - use redeem(collateralAsset, naraUsdAmount, allowQueue) instead      - maxDeposit() and maxMint() reflect per-block limits and paused state      - maxWithdraw() and maxRedeem() return 0 (ERC4626 withdraw/redeem are unsupported)      - preview* functions account for fees but the corresponding actions may be disabledIMPORTANT - Redemption Mechanism: The "redemption queue" is NOT an ordered FIFO queue.      It is implemented as a per-user mapping (one active request per user). There is no global      ordering, no "next in line" concept, and no automatic FIFO processing. Completion order is      discretionary by the COLLATERAL_MANAGER_ROLE (solver), who can complete requests opportunistically      via completeRedeem() or bulkCompleteRedeem() when liquidity becomes available.This contract is upgradeable using UUPS proxy patternPrivileged roles: - DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE: Full administrative control. Can:   - Upgrade contract implementation (UUPS)   - Set all configuration parameters (fees, limits, minimums, treasury, Keyring config)   - Redistribute locked amounts from blacklisted users   - Grant/revoke all other roles - GATEKEEPER_ROLE: Emergency controls. Can:   - Pause/unpause all operations - COLLATERAL_MANAGER_ROLE: Manages redemption queue execution. Can:   - Complete queued redemptions (completeRedeem, bulkCompleteRedeem)   - Acts as "solver" to process escrowed redemption requests when liquidity becomes available   - Completion order is discretionary (not FIFO) - can complete any user's request opportunistically - MINTER_ROLE: Can mint NaraUSD without collateral backing (for incentives, etc.) - BLACKLIST_MANAGER_ROLE: Can add/remove addresses from blacklist (FULL_RESTRICTED_ROLE) - FULL_RESTRICTED_ROLE: Restriction status (not an operator role). Addresses with this role:   - Cannot transfer tokens (including via transferFrom)   - Cannot mint or redeem   - Can have their locked balances redistributed by admin

There is no global ordering, no "next in line",      and completion order is discretionary by COLLATERAL_MANAGER_ROLE (solver). The solver can complete      any user's request opportunistically when liquidity becomes available.Note: Users can repeatedly create and cancel requests (spam is possible but costs gas).The minRedeemAmount check is enforced only at request creation time.      Queued requests are "grandfathered" and will complete even if minRedeemAmount is increased later.IMPORTANT - Asset Removal Risk: If governance removes a collateral asset from MCT's supported      assets list while redemption requests are queued for that asset, those queued requests will      become non-completable (completion requires asset to be supported in MCT). However, users can      ALWAYS call cancelRedeem() to recover their escrowed NaraUSD regardless of asset support status.      Users should monitor asset support changes for queued requests. Governance should ensure queued      requests are completed or users are notified before removing asset support.

devdoc.details: Users stake NaraUSD tokens and earn rewards. The contract uses ERC4626 standard      for vault operations and can be integrated with LayerZero's OVault for omnichain functionality.      Rewards are distributed by REWARDER_ROLE and vest over time to prevent MEV attacks.If cooldown duration is set to zero, the NaraUSDPlus behavior follows ERC4626 standard      and disables cooldownShares and cooldownAssets methods. Can:   - Pause/unpause contract operations - REWARDER_ROLE: Reward operations. Can:   - Transfer in staking rewards (vested)   - Burn NaraUSD assets from the contract (deflationary action) - BLACKLIST_MANAGER_ROLE: Restriction controls. Can:   - Add/remove FULL_RESTRICTED_STAKER_ROLE on addresses - FULL_RESTRICTED_STAKER_ROLE: Restriction status (not an operator role).      * @dev Sets `value` as the allowance of `spender` over ``owner``'s tokens,
     * given ``owner``'s signed approval.
     *
     * IMPORTANT: The same issues {IERC20-approve} has related to transaction
     * ordering also apply here.
     *
     * Emits an {Approval} event.
     *
     * Requirements:
     *
     * - `spender` cannot be the zero address.
     * - `deadline` must be a timestamp in the future.
     * - `v`, `r` and `s` must be a valid `secp256k1` signature from `owner`
     * over the EIP712-formatted function arguments.
     * - the signature must use ``owner``'s current nonce (see {nonces}).
     *
     * For more information on the signature format, see the
     * https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612#specification[relevant EIP
     * section].
     *
     * CAUTION: See Security Considerations above.
     */
    function permit(
        address owner,
        address spender,
        uint256 value,
        uint256 deadline,
        uint8 v,
        bytes32 r,
        bytes32 s
    ) external;

    /**
     * @dev Returns the current nonce for `owner`. This value must be
     * included whenever a signature is generated for {permit}.
     *
     * Every successful call to {permit} increases ``owner``'s nonce by one. This
     * prevents a signature from being used multiple times.
     */
    function nonces(address owner) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @dev Returns the domain separator used in the encoding of the signature for {permit}, as defined by {EIP712}.
     */
    // solhint-disable-next-line func-name-mixedcase
    function DOMAIN_SEPARATOR() external view returns (bytes32);
}

devdoc.details: Users stake NaraUSD tokens and earn rewards. The contract uses ERC4626 standard      for vault operations and can be integrated with LayerZero's OVault for omnichain functionality.      Rewards are distributed by REWARDER_ROLE and vest over time to prevent MEV attacks.If cooldown duration is set to zero, the NaraUSDPlus behavior follows ERC4626 standard      and disables cooldownShares and cooldownAssets methods. If cooldown duration is greater      than zero, the ERC4626 withdrawal and redeem functions are disabled, breaking the ERC4626      standard, and enabling the cooldownShares and the cooldownAssets functions.Privileged roles: - DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE: Full administrative control. Can:   - Upgrade contract implementation (UUPS)   - Set core configuration (cooldown duration, vesting period)   - Rescue non-asset tokens from the contract   - Redistribute locked balances from restricted users   - Grant/revoke all other roles - GATEKEEPER_ROLE: Emergency controls. Can:   - Pause/unpause contract operations - REWARDER_ROLE: Reward operations. Can:   - Transfer in staking rewards (vested)   - Burn NaraUSD assets from the contract (deflationary action) - BLACKLIST_MANAGER_ROLE: Restriction controls. Can:   - Add/remove FULL_RESTRICTED_STAKER_ROLE on addresses - FULL_RESTRICTED_STAKER_ROLE: Restriction status (not an operator role). Addresses with this role:   - Cannot transfer tokens (including via transferFrom)   - Cannot stake, cooldown, or unstake   - Can have locked balances redistributed by adminThis contract is upgradeable using UUPS proxy pattern

Ethereum NaraUSD primary collateral mint/redemption and NaraUSD+ staking only, not BSC bridge tokens, Port/third-party vault curation, issuer minting, rewards management, permits or roles. Current implementation slots observed at block 26257645: NaraUSD 0x87cf5006e1cbf0d35c622c5f1be891b2f71878ea; NaraUSD+ 0x9e1d521894c45fa26e0f06809674037c78e3c1b3. UUPS roles, collateral/MCT, Keyring and silo controls are mutable.

Primary mint/redeem is for Authorized Users under KYC/KYB and configured Keyring credentials/whitelist; blacklists and pause apply. Catalog admission grants no credential, role, approval or legal access. Staking deposits are permissionless subject to blacklist/pause and source minimum-share constraints.

NaraUSD mint pulls supported collateral from msg.sender and mints only to msg.sender through MCT. Redemption burns caller NaraUSD and pays caller selected collateral; allowQueue=false reverts if liquidity is insufficient. Native collateral decimals are normalized to 18; division truncates. Mutable percentage/minimum fees, minimum amounts and per-block limits apply; no caller min-output/deadline parameter exists.

Queued redemption locks caller NaraUSD in the redeem silo; one request per address, NOT a FIFO queue despite primary documentation describing ordered service. Manager can complete opportunistically; caller tryCompleteRedeem can complete own request if liquidity/caps permit. Completion burns escrow and pays caller at current fees; it does not recheck Keyring expiry. Asset removal can block completion. cancelRedeem returns escrow subject to pause/blacklist; updateRedemptionRequest funds/refunds the difference without changing asset. No payout date is guaranteed.

NaraUSD+ deposit/mint pulls caller NaraUSD and issues shares to receiver; 18-decimal underlying/shares, balance-minus-unvested-rewards ERC4626 exchange rate with virtual offsets. Deposit floors shares; mint rounds required assets up. NAV/income originates from offchain payment-financing operations and maker/reviewer/executor controls, not autonomous proof of portfolio value; insurance then staked shares absorb losses, and principal can be lost.

NaraUSD+ cooldown was 604800 seconds (7 days) and both proxies paused=false at the observed block, not continuing availability. Direct withdraw/redeem is structurally disabled while cooldown is nonzero and excluded. cooldownAssets rounds shares up; cooldownShares locks exact caller shares. Both transfer shares into silo and adding to an existing cooldown resets unlock for ALL locked shares. Assets returned by preview are not a fixed future entitlement; shares continue rate exposure until unstake burns at claim-time rate to receiver. cancelCooldown returns locked shares.

Queue and cooldown ledgers explicitly narrow amounts to uint152; callers must keep queued/updated/aggregate locked share amounts within that range. Minimum-share invariants can prevent dust exits. unstake has no top-level pause modifier but calls _withdraw, which enforces pause/blacklists/nonzero/minimum shares. No silo administrative or direct transfer method is admitted.

Primary docs target redemption within 7 days but mention pressure up to roughly 90 days; these are not contract-enforced completion promises. Credit, reserve mix, custody, offchain settlement, mutable fees, freezes and legal/operational loss risks remain. Source and ABI review proves none of the portfolio, backing, yield or solvency claims.

Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory; zero native value required.

Ethereum NaraUSD primary collateral mint/redemption and NaraUSD+ staking only, not BSC bridge tokens, Port/third-party vault curation, issuer minting, rewards management, permits or roles. Current implementation slots observed at block 26257645: NaraUSD 0x87cf5006e1cbf0d35c622c5f1be891b2f71878ea; NaraUSD+ 0x9e1d521894c45fa26e0f06809674037c78e3c1b3. UUPS roles, collateral/MCT, Keyring and silo controls are mutable.

Primary mint/redeem is for Authorized Users under KYC/KYB and configured Keyring credentials/whitelist; blacklists and pause apply. Catalog admission grants no credential, role, approval or legal access. Staking deposits are permissionless subject to blacklist/pause and source minimum-share constraints.

NaraUSD mint pulls supported collateral from msg.sender and mints only to msg.sender through MCT. Redemption burns caller NaraUSD and pays caller selected collateral; allowQueue=false reverts if liquidity is insufficient. Native collateral decimals are normalized to 18; division truncates. Mutable percentage/minimum fees, minimum amounts and per-block limits apply; no caller min-output/deadline parameter exists.

Queued redemption locks caller NaraUSD in the redeem silo; one request per address, NOT a FIFO queue despite primary documentation describing ordered service. Manager can complete opportunistically; caller tryCompleteRedeem can complete own request if liquidity/caps permit. Completion burns escrow and pays caller at current fees; it does not recheck Keyring expiry. Asset removal can block completion. cancelRedeem returns escrow subject to pause/blacklist; updateRedemptionRequest funds/refunds the difference without changing asset. No payout date is guaranteed.

NaraUSD+ deposit/mint pulls caller NaraUSD and issues shares to receiver; 18-decimal underlying/shares, balance-minus-unvested-rewards ERC4626 exchange rate with virtual offsets. Deposit floors shares; mint rounds required assets up. NAV/income originates from offchain payment-financing operations and maker/reviewer/executor controls, not autonomous proof of portfolio value; insurance then staked shares absorb losses, and principal can be lost.

NaraUSD+ cooldown was 604800 seconds (7 days) and both proxies paused=false at the observed block, not continuing availability. Direct withdraw/redeem is structurally disabled while cooldown is nonzero and excluded. cooldownAssets rounds shares up; cooldownShares locks exact caller shares. Both transfer shares into silo and adding to an existing cooldown resets unlock for ALL locked shares. Assets returned by preview are not a fixed future entitlement; shares continue rate exposure until unstake burns at claim-time rate to receiver. cancelCooldown returns locked shares.

Queue and cooldown ledgers explicitly narrow amounts to uint152; callers must keep queued/updated/aggregate locked share amounts within that range. Minimum-share invariants can prevent dust exits. unstake has no top-level pause modifier but calls _withdraw, which enforces pause/blacklists/nonzero/minimum shares. No silo administrative or direct transfer method is admitted.

Primary docs target redemption within 7 days but mention pressure up to roughly 90 days; these are not contract-enforced completion promises. Credit, reserve mix, custody, offchain settlement, mutable fees, freezes and legal/operational loss risks remain. Source and ABI review proves none of the portfolio, backing, yield or solvency claims.
